# Sandbox Specification

A sandbox, written down: each section one grant, and everything it leaves out closed. The `sandbox` specification is TOML, given to a command that reads it as a file, and a field flag sets the field it names, overriding the file. Its JSON Schema is [`sandbox.schema.json`](sandbox.schema.json).

## Use It

Give `lnk agent harness-permission add`, `lnk agent harness-permission remove`, `lnk agent permission add`, `lnk agent permission remove`, `lnk sandbox check`, `lnk sandbox learn`, and `lnk sandbox run` a `sandbox` specification as a file, and set any field below with its field flag, which overrides the file. `lnk sandbox spec show` prints the specification as it is read.

## Every Option

Every field the reader takes, with an example value.

```toml
kind = "sandbox"
schema = 1
name = "app"
version = 1

[browser]
hosts = ["github.com"]

[browser.linux]
hosts = ["github.com"]

[browser.macos]
hosts = ["github.com"]

[commands]
allow = [
    "sh",
    "git",
    "/usr/lib/git-core/",
]
developer_tools = true
toolchains = [
    "rust",
    "git",
]

[commands.linux]
allow = [
    "sh",
    "git",
    "/usr/lib/git-core/",
]
developer_tools = true
toolchains = [
    "rust",
    "git",
]

[commands.macos]
allow = [
    "sh",
    "git",
    "/usr/lib/git-core/",
]
developer_tools = true
toolchains = [
    "rust",
    "git",
]

[files]
hide = ["~/code/app/secrets"]
read = ["~/Documents/reports"]
write = ["~/code/app"]
write_dot_files = ["~/code/app"]

[files.linux]
hide = ["~/code/app/secrets"]
read = ["~/Documents/reports"]
write = ["~/code/app"]
write_dot_files = ["~/code/app"]

[files.macos]
hide = ["~/code/app/secrets"]
read = ["~/Documents/reports"]
write = ["~/code/app"]
write_dot_files = ["~/code/app"]

[internet]
hosts = [
    "api.openai.com",
    "github.com",
]
per_minute = 600
tcp = ["github.com:22"]

[internet.linux]
hosts = [
    "api.openai.com",
    "github.com",
]
per_minute = 600
tcp = ["github.com:22"]

[internet.macos]
hosts = [
    "api.openai.com",
    "github.com",
]
per_minute = 600
tcp = ["github.com:22"]

[lan]
hosts = [
    "nas.local",
    "192.168.1.0/24",
]

[lan.linux]
hosts = [
    "nas.local",
    "192.168.1.0/24",
]

[lan.macos]
hosts = [
    "nas.local",
    "192.168.1.0/24",
]

[localhost]
models = [11434]
ports = [8080]

[localhost.linux]
models = [11434]
ports = [8080]

[localhost.macos]
models = [11434]
ports = [8080]

[network]
mode = "proxy"

[network.linux]
mode = "proxy"

[network.macos]
mode = "proxy"

[tools]
names = ["gh"]

[tools.linux]
names = ["gh"]

[tools.macos]
names = ["gh"]
```

## `browser`

> **Type** a table · **Flag** `--browser`

Pages it may ask you to open in your browser, asking you each time. A
section needs `hosts`.

### `hosts`

> **Type** a list, each text · **Flag** `--browser.hosts`

Hosts a page may be on, or `["*"]` for any.

### `linux`

> **Type** a table · **Flag** `--browser.linux`

Linux's own keys for this section: each one given replaces the section's there.

### `macos`

> **Type** a table · **Flag** `--browser.macos`

macOS's own keys for this section: each one given replaces the section's there.

## `commands`

> **Type** a table · **Flag** `--commands`

The programs it may run: a section needs `allow` or
`toolchains`, and with a specification one left out runs nothing.

### `allow`

> **Type** a list, each text · **Flag** `--commands.allow`

Programs, folders of them ending `/`, or `["*"]` for any.

A program is a name on `PATH` or a path. `["*"]` stands alone.

### `developer_tools`

> **Type** `true` or `false` · **Flag** `--commands.developer_tools`

`true`: Xcode's and the Command Line Tools' programs.

They're read only and may run, so git and compilers run, on macOS; it
means nothing elsewhere.

### `linux`

> **Type** a table · **Flag** `--commands.linux`

Linux's own keys for this section: each one given replaces the section's there.

### `macos`

> **Type** a table · **Flag** `--commands.macos`

macOS's own keys for this section: each one given replaces the section's there.

### `toolchains`

> **Type** a list, each one of `shell`, `git`, `rust`, `node`, `python`, `go`, `c`, `desktop`, `jvm` · **Flag** `--commands.toolchains`

Toolchains, each standing for the programs it names (`lnk sandbox permission list` lists each one's programs).

A toolchain also runs the programs its own programs keep, and those a
build writes under the folders it writes, such as Rust's build scripts.

- `shell`: A shell and the everyday programs a script runs
- `git`: Git, with its own programs and ssh, which it runs for a remote
- `rust`: Rust: Cargo, rustc and rust-analyzer, with rustup's toolchains, the linker, proc-macro servers, and a build's scripts and tests
- `node`: Node.js and its package managers (npm, pnpm, Yarn, Bun), with a package's commands
- `python`: Python and its project tools (pip, uv, Poetry, tox), with a virtual environment's programs
- `go`: Go, its language server and golangci-lint
- `c`: C and C++ compilers, make, CMake and Ninja, Valgrind, and clangd
- `desktop`: An X server with no screen (Xvfb), and the keymap compiler and shell it runs
- `jvm`: Java and Kotlin, their builds (Gradle, Maven), and their language servers

## `files`

> **Type** a table · **Flag** `--files`

Your folders it reads and writes: a section needs `write` or `read`.
`read = ["~"]` is your whole home, never Link's settings, and a
project's dot files that run outside (`.git` among them) stay read only
unless `write_dot_files` names their folder.

### `hide`

> **Type** a list, each text · **Flag** `--files.hide`

Folders closed whatever else opens them.

The folders of `write` and `read` in them stay open, and it adds
up across the default table, an OS's and the flags.

### `linux`

> **Type** a table · **Flag** `--files.linux`

Linux's own keys for this section: each one given replaces the section's there, but `hide`, which adds up.

### `macos`

> **Type** a table · **Flag** `--files.macos`

macOS's own keys for this section: each one given replaces the section's there, but `hide`, which adds up.

### `read`

> **Type** a list, each text · **Flag** `--files.read`

Folders it reads; `"~"`, your whole home.

### `write`

> **Type** a list, each text · **Flag** `--files.write`

Folders it reads and writes.

### `write_dot_files`

> **Type** a list, each text · **Flag** `--files.write_dot_files`

Folders of `write` whose outside dot files it writes too.

Those are the dot files that run outside the sandbox: `.git`,
`.envrc`, `.vscode` and `.idea`.

## `internet`

> **Type** a table · **Flag** `--internet`

Public hosts it reaches, through Link's proxy and logged; never this
machine or its network. A section needs `hosts`.

### `hosts`

> **Type** a list, each text · **Flag** `--internet.hosts`

Hosts, or `["*"]` for any public host.

Each is a name (`api.openai.com`), the names under one
(`*.github.com`) or an address.

### `linux`

> **Type** a table · **Flag** `--internet.linux`

Linux's own keys for this section: each one given replaces the section's there.

### `macos`

> **Type** a table · **Flag** `--internet.macos`

macOS's own keys for this section: each one given replaces the section's there.

### `per_minute`

> **Type** a whole number from 0 · **Flag** `--internet.per_minute`

A whole number, at least 1: the most calls a minute.

### `tcp`

> **Type** a list, each text · **Flag** `--internet.tcp`

`host:port` endpoints it reaches beyond HTTPS and HTTP.

## `lan`

> **Type** a table · **Flag** `--lan`

Other machines of your network it reaches, through Link's proxy; never
this machine or a cloud's metadata service. A section needs `hosts`.

### `hosts`

> **Type** a list, each text · **Flag** `--lan.hosts`

Hosts, or `["*"]` for the private ranges.

Each is a name, an address or a range (`192.168.1.0/24`).

### `linux`

> **Type** a table · **Flag** `--lan.linux`

Linux's own keys for this section: each one given replaces the section's there.

### `macos`

> **Type** a table · **Flag** `--lan.macos`

macOS's own keys for this section: each one given replaces the section's there.

## `localhost`

> **Type** a table · **Flag** `--localhost`

Servers on this machine it calls, each port named; a model's for
inference only. A section needs `ports` or `models`.

### `linux`

> **Type** a table · **Flag** `--localhost.linux`

Linux's own keys for this section: each one given replaces the section's there.

### `macos`

> **Type** a table · **Flag** `--localhost.macos`

macOS's own keys for this section: each one given replaces the section's there.

### `models`

> **Type** a list, each a whole number from 0 · **Flag** `--localhost.models`

Ports of local model runtimes, for inference only.

Each is reached through the proxy, never as a raw port; alone, the
section needs no `ports`.

### `ports`

> **Type** a list, each one of `*`, or a whole number from 0 · **Flag** `--localhost.ports`

Port numbers, or `["*"]` for every port.

`["*"]` only with `[network] mode = "host"`. Left out, only
`models` are reached.

## `name`

> **Type** text · **Flag** `--spec.name`

Text: what it's called, to tell specifications apart.

## `network`

> **Type** a table · **Flag** `--network`

How it reaches the network: through Link's filtering proxy, the default,
or this machine's network as it is, with no proxy between.

### `linux`

> **Type** a table · **Flag** `--network.linux`

Linux's own keys for this section: each one given replaces the section's there.

### `macos`

> **Type** a table · **Flag** `--network.macos`

macOS's own keys for this section: each one given replaces the section's there.

### `mode`

> **Type** one of `proxy`, `host` · **Flag** `--network.mode`

`"proxy"`, the default, or `"host"`, with no proxy.

`"host"` is this machine's network as it is, so nothing is
filtered or logged and the sections a proxy carries are refused
beside it; of the loopback, every port on Linux, `[localhost]
ports` on macOS.

## `teams`

> **Type** a table by name, each a table · **Unavailable** a grant from the program that starts the sandbox, which a sandbox run of its own refuses · **Flag** `--teams`

Of each shared folder it reaches, by the folder's name, what it
writes and only reads; one not here it can't reach. Only the program
that starts the sandbox knows where each shared folder is, so it's
that program's grant, and a sandbox run of its own refuses it.

### `<name>`

> **Type** a table · **Flag** `--teams.<name>`

What of a shared folder the sandbox may reach: folders of it it
writes, and those it only reads, each a folder's name in it (`drafts`),
or `.` for the whole folder. The rest of it is closed.

#### `read`

> **Type** a list, each text · **Default** `[]` · **Flag** `--teams.<name>.read`

Folders of the shared folder it only reads.

#### `write`

> **Type** a list, each text · **Default** `[]` · **Flag** `--teams.<name>.write`

Folders of the shared folder it reads and writes, each a
folder's name in it, or `.` for all of it.

## `tools`

> **Type** a table · **Flag** `--tools`

Your tools from `lnk sandbox tool add`, MCP tools which run outside the
sandbox with your logins, asking you. A section needs `names`.

### `linux`

> **Type** a table · **Flag** `--tools.linux`

Linux's own keys for this section: each one given replaces the section's there.

### `macos`

> **Type** a table · **Flag** `--tools.macos`

macOS's own keys for this section: each one given replaces the section's there.

### `names`

> **Type** a list, each text · **Flag** `--tools.names`

Your tools' names, as `lnk sandbox tool add` named them.

## `version`

> **Type** a whole number from 0 · **Flag** `--spec.version`

A whole number, yours to bump when you change it.
